threeQuestionGate.whatExecutesTheEtjStateOnThePdf: resolveEtjDetermination in packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/etj-determination.ts — ONE implementation, called once from report-model.ts's composeParcelReportFacts. It takes (the engine's city-limits reading, the etjStatus rail's answer, the unslated fallback reason) and returns the four-state determination plus the carried fact, the declared conflict and the reason. pdf/feasibility.ts's etjFactChip/etjConsequenceSentence and report-model.ts's jurisdictionActionSentence/jurisdictionSkeletonSentence only READ the composed model; none of them re-derives a state. The rail answer itself comes from recordEtjStatusAnswer (parcel-record-reader-client.ts), which reuses the P-302 recordRailAnswer three-way rule.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: The retrieval service's `etjStatus` rail — already declared on both sides (rail-keys.ts:43, retrieval-api's parcel-record-rail-registry.ts:54), reading `excluded-mid-cutover` today, and written by P-336. For a parcel whose rail serves `record`, the cell's value/absence kind decides the reading: a state string, a determination object, a declared conflict object, or an `absent-verified` cell (promoted to ETJ `absent`). Everything else — an unslated rail, a refusal, `not-applicable`, a malformed payload, no reader at all, a failed fetch — resolves to `unresolved` WITH a reason, and the three 'no determination in hand at all' paths render the pre-change sentence byte for byte so no county's document changes before P-336 applies.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenThePdfAndThePanelDisagree: TODAY: nothing — that was the defect. What this lane ADDS: (a) the PDF no longer asserts a state it does not have, so a parcel whose rail has not answered says `unresolved` + why rather than a fabricated `present`/`absent`; (b) within the engine's own surfaces, the PDF and the narrative read ONE composed value, so the fact sheet and the narrative cannot disagree with each other — before this lane they could only agree because both were the same literal; (c) a declared conflict is a SERVED STATE rather than a hidden disagreement, so `incorporated` + `present` cannot be printed as a clean pair; (d) the cross-repo agreement is a named, exported literal set plus a behaviour matrix for P-331's drift check. What still does NOT fail: nothing in the engine compares its own read against the panel's live read, and the rail's own writer is P-336 — so a ledger cell that is WRONG (rather than unreadable) is forwarded as-is. That is deliberate: P-332's rule 3 says the determination is read, never derived, and which of the two reads is wrong for a live conflict is a store question that etj-determination.ts's header deliberately does not decide in code.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesIt: Named rather than assumed: (a) the MCP / card / share surfaces in hauska-map — P-332 shipped the panel's four states and P-336 makes the cells serve; the PDF is now the third surface reading the same rail, and the probe in leave_behind is what checks the agreement after the deploy; (b) cortex-api's narrative path — the jurisdiction object is SPREAD into the LDT narrative payload, so the new fields ride along inside an object that was already sent; whether cortex tolerates the extra keys is NOT measured by this lane (no deploy, no live call) and is named in openAtCP2; (c) any OTHER engine surface rendering jurisdiction — bounded by CP1's census: the token appears in exactly the six production sites listed and ONE PDF row prints ETJ.
